title: CatBoost model predicts occult lymph node metastasis in early lung cancer
summary: Among 12 machine-learning algorithms using 46 preoperative features, a 10-feature CatBoost model predicted occult lymph node metastasis in clinical T1N0 NSCLC with consolidation-to-tumour ratio above 0.5. Occult metastasis occurred in 16.5% of 1,784 development patients and 18.5% of 525 external patients, with AUC 0.870 (0.827-0.906) internally and 0.855 (0.814-0.895) externally, and SHAP explained features. External calibration overestimated risk at intermediate-to-high probabilities, and prospective validation is required.
ai_technology: CatBoost gradient boosting selected among 12 machine-learning algorithms, with SHAP attribution

evidence.unknown: Clinical utility for guiding nodal dissection; full text not reviewed.
